rv.q: The first half's weightless, larky sitcom style gives way to an oddly dead atmosphere that lacks the air of a great tragedy.
This play has not simply been dusted off; it is a classic and has been well thought out.
For those near Liverpool, this is definitely not one to miss.
Once again, Death to the Salesman returns to the stage- full of light, music and lively energy- and I think it's safe to say, extremely far from dull.
The cultural reimagining works because it illuminates ideas that were already present in Miller's play.
Death of a Salesman is a night not to be missed with a whole host of accompanying events to immerse you into this Afro-centric retelling.

cn.t: This Afrocentric Scouse revival finds fresh layers in Miller's classic by centering the immigrant experience, earning strong praise for its sense of place and identity, though one critic remains less convinced by the approach.
